shipments.t: A departed guest's bill is final
ships: NOTHING IN THIS BUILD WRITES folios.status, AND TWELVE FUNCTIONS GUARD ON IT. Measured, not inferred: the only function that updates folios at all is reverse_checkout, which sets the status back to 'open'; check_out_booking moves the BOOKING to checked_out and leaves the folio alone; every live folio is 'open'

TESTED BY BEHAVIOUR on a booking checked in and checked out, in a rolled-back transaction. ADD A CHARGE: ACCEPTED. TAKE A PAYMENT: ACCEPTED. APPLY A DISCOUNT: ACCEPTED. REVERSE A CHARGE: ACCEPTED. REFUND MONEY: ACCEPTED. A guest who departed last week can still have their bill changed five different ways, and twelve functions READ as though they prevent it

THE GUARDS MAKE IT WORSE THAN NO GUARDS, which is why this is not an unreachable edge. Machinery promising a state transition nothing performs is rule 28 at the level of a subsystem: the guards are what stops anybody asking the question, and every week it stays unwired another one gets written against a status nothing writes — multiplying the false comfort rather than the protection

So: check_out_booking settles the folio, with the rule for WHEN a folio may be settled (an outstanding balance? a credit balance?) decided rather than implied; a deliberate, audited re-open; and the twelve guards verified to fire by behaviour rather than by reading, each with its own assertion

AND IT IS STAGE 1, NOT STAGE 4. Stage 1 is close what is already open, and 0.8 already claims checkout completes the bill while the lifecycle sits half built. Cashiering is about who holds the money, not about whether a bill is final
shipments.proof: Check a guest out. Then try to add a charge, take a payment, apply a discount, reverse a charge and refund money on that folio: each one refused, by name, naming the remedy. Then re-open the folio deliberately and watch all five become possible again, with the re-opening on the record.
shipments.note: FOUND WHILE CENSUSING PIN ORDERING FOR 069, as the answer to 'is this precondition reachable?' — and the answer was that it is not, because the state it tests is never created. 069 reordered the guards anyway so this shipment does not also have to remember to. One of them was decoration and the breakage proved it — an em-dash assertion stayed GREEN with the blank restored, because the fixture already had a dash in its reason column; it was rebuilt on a fixture where the cost cell is the only thing that can produce one. The typeahead work made the same mistake twice more and both were caught by breaking the code: an assertion that typed into an opened picker passed under the defect, because opening had already loaded a starting set and the panel was showing stale rows rather than reaching the empty branch; and the close() reset was proven on a fixture where it was not load-bearing, until it was rebuilt on a picker whose source is genuinely empty. 47 picker assertions, all three breakages red.
shipments.note: Eight findings from the first live walk of Purchases and Suppliers, signed in as the owner against the real database. The first is the whole shipment's weight: 98 refusals across the migrations raise insufficient_privilege and 25 carry a hand-written hint, and every one of those 25 reached the user as "You do not have permission to make this change." That is the 1.1c lesson at the generic layer — stockErrorMessage was fixed to stop swallowing hints and errors.ts, which ninety-odd surfaces call, was left doing exactly that. The second is a promise the product was not keeping: the PIN dialog tells a manager the approval is recorded against them by name, permanently, and it was — in a column no screen displayed, and in a provenance report whose three sections all ask whether stock arrived in the right PLACE rather than in the right QUANTITY. Phone width was found in the same walk and is deliberately NOT here: see 1.1a2. The typeahead IS here, because it is a walk finding and this is the shipment that fixes walk findings — and because it is the same defect class as the first two: a screen stating something untrue with confidence. It lives in the shared Typeahead, so it was fixed and proved at the primitive; a proof written against the supplier screen would have proved one caller and left the item, location and account pickers telling the same lie.

shipments.t: The purchasing screens on a phone
ships: One DataTable primitive: a column spec declared ONCE per table, rendered as the table it always was above md and as a card per row below it
All SEVEN purchasing tables through it — the receive form first, because that is the one somebody uses standing at a store door
useIsNarrow on Tailwind's existing md (768px), chosen in JavaScript rather than CSS so there is exactly one input per field at any width
On a phone every cell of a row is in one card: the item name, the quantity box and the reason box cannot be separated by any scroll position
The mandatory reason sits in that card beside the quantity it explains, appearing the moment a difference exists and never behind a disclosure
A cell with nothing to say is omitted from the card rather than printed as a label with nothing after it
The three Provenance tables too, on the follow-up ruling: same shape, same primitive, and one of them was the over-receipt table 049 had just added
shipments.proof: proofs/narrowTableRender drives the real ReceiveLinesTable at both widths and asserts CONTAINMENT rather than pixels — happy-dom does no layout, so "992px in 295px" is not provable from a proof and stays a live check. 15 assertions. Broken three ways: rendering one table at every width (the markup this replaced) turns 8 red including the containment one; rendering cards at every width turns the four wide-screen assertions red; printing a label for an empty cell turns the last one red. Live at 375px with the card photographed for the record: zero page overflow, card 33-327 inside the viewport, every right-aligned value ending at 315, five inputs inside the rice card including the required reason.
shipments.note: MEASURED ON THE LIVE WALK, NOT ESTIMATED. The receive table rendered 992px of content inside a 295px window: 697px, two and a third screens, off to the right. At rest not one input was visible and the screen read as a list of what was ordered followed by a Note box. The first column was not sticky, so scrolling right to reach the Arrived boxes took the item names away and left unlabelled fields. Item sat at 40-289 and Reason at 922-992, so they could never be on screen together at any scroll position — and Reason is the column the server REQUIRES on a short delivery. The sequence on a phone was therefore: type a quantity, press Record delivery, read a refusal asking for a reason, go looking 922px to the right for the field. THE COUNT IN THE ORIGINAL NOTE WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE: it said four tables, because four were measured in one sitting. Purchasing has SEVEN (receive 62rem, Purchases list 54rem, deliveries 52rem, order form 48rem, supplier activity 46rem, order lines 44rem, suppliers list 44rem) and all seven are through the primitive. ONE PRIMITIVE RATHER THAN SEVEN FIXES, on the ruling's own reasoning: the reason seven tables shared one defect is that they were written seven times, and converting some now would leave somebody re-deciding the column spec later with less context, with the odd one out being the one nobody tests. THE BREAKPOINT IS JAVASCRIPT, which is the arguable part, and the argument is in hooks/useIsNarrow: a card is a regrouping rather than a restack so CSS cannot produce it; two of these tables carry headers a data-label string cannot hold; and rendering both shapes and hiding one would put every input in the document twice, which is unacceptable on a form. THE THREE PROVENANCE TABLES WENT THROUGH TOO (52, 56 and 48rem), on a follow-up ruling after they were raised rather than swept in. They are read-only, so the consequence on a phone was annoyance rather than danger, but leaving the newest of them — the over-receipt table 049 had just added — as the odd one out would have been the exact failure the one-primitive argument is about. They keep their own look (text-xs, a divided tbody, a heavier header) through two class hooks on the primitive, and the phone proof asserts that, because a primitive that hard-coded purchasing's classes would quietly restyle a screen nobody asked to change. Everything else in the app is counted in 1.1a3.

shipments.t: Every other table on a phone
ships: The three storekeeper tables that are unconditionally too wide, through the DataTable primitive: ProductsTable (64rem), ItemMovementLedger (40rem), StockItemLedger (34rem)
A decision on the five inventory tables that escape their min-width below sm but still cramp — convert, or leave and say why
Nothing else, unless the §0 below turns out to be wrong about who uses what
shipments.proof: At 360px a storekeeper can read the item catalogue and one item's movement history without scrolling sideways, and the phone proof covers at least one of the three the way it already covers the receive form and the over-receipt report.
shipments.note: THE §0 COUNT, RUN BEFORE DECIDING ANYTHING. Twenty-two table elements exist outside purchasing and provenance, which is more than either of us expected — and the set that MATTERS is three, which is the point of counting rather than converting on principle. GROUP A, an unconditional min-width that forces sideways scrolling at 360px (11): ProductsTable 64rem/1024px, ProductImportScreen 46rem, StockImportScreen 44rem, ItemMovementLedger 40rem, StockItemLedger 34rem, ChartOfAccountsTab 34rem, RoomTypeStep 32rem, BookingsTable 960px, AccountsPanel 560px, StayTab 22rem/352px (fits at 360), GuestStaysTable 11rem and FolioBill 8rem (both fit). GROUP B, written as sm:min-w-[...] so there is NO min-width below 640px (5, all inventory): CountSheet 32rem, CountVarianceReport 44rem, MovementsList 48rem, NegativeStockTab 48rem, StockTakeTab 40rem. Somebody already made a deliberate decision on these — they do not overflow on a phone, they cramp. That is a different problem and may not need this fix. GROUP C, no min-width at all (6): GuestLedger, StatementDocument, FactTable, Markdown and the two tables on StockCountPrintPage. FactTable is a label/value table by design, Markdown renders the staff guide, and the print page is paper — none is a phone screen. WHO ACTUALLY WORKS ON A PHONE decides the scope, not the widths. A storekeeper and a housekeeper do; the front desk sits at a desk. So of the 11 in group A, only THREE are both storekeeper-facing and unconditionally over-wide: ProductsTable (the worst in the app at 1024px, and the one a storekeeper opens most), ItemMovementLedger and StockItemLedger. BookingsTable at 960px is the second-widest table in the product and is front-desk work, so it is deliberately NOT in scope. The two import previews are desk work by their nature — somebody uploading a spreadsheet is sitting down. HOUSEKEEPING HAS NO TABLES YET: the module is SOON in the nav. When it lands it is phone-first by role, and it should use the primitive from its first commit rather than joining a list like this one later.

shipments.t: Stock take as a real count
ships: BLIND count: the counter types what they physically counted and sees nothing else — expected quantity and variance appear only after submitting
stock_takes and stock_take_lines, with expected quantity snapshotted at the moment the count starts
start, record line, finish RPCs with idempotency keys and the posting-lock check
A resumable sheet: a count can be left open and finished later, by the same person or another
Partial counts allowed — a location does not have to be counted whole
Variance above a threshold needs a manager PIN to finish, same pattern as discounts
The count_adjustment write path, finally used for what it was declared for
The count is its own page (/inventory/counts/<id>), no tab strip to lose it by clicking — linkable, refreshable, printable
Print the count sheet in a clean tab: hotel name, count number, location, date, every shelf, a ruled box to write in, notes and signature lines — blind while open because it reads the same view
Accordion: Still to count and Already counted, paging independently
Kebab per row and on the count: carry on, print, open the report, undo

Undo a finished count reverses every movement it posted, manager PIN at any size, reason mandatory — there is no delete, because deleting the record would delete the evidence that stock moved and a manager approved it
Finishing warns once when stock moved in the location while the count ran AND the affected items were counted after it moved — the double-count case a snapshot cannot see
shipments.proof: Start a count, post a receipt for a counted item mid-count, finish, and the variance reflects the snapshot rather than the receipt. Refresh mid-count and the sheet comes back. Confirm the expected quantity is not present in the page payload before submission, not merely hidden in the UI.
shipments.note: Blind is the whole point: if the counter can see what the system expects, they write that number down and the count proves nothing. Postings are deliberately NOT blocked during a count — the 1.1b snapshot is what makes that safe. Today the count lives entirely in component state, the on-hand figure is grabbed per keystroke, and a refresh loses everything. 039 and 040 both PUSHED. 040 added the count-reversal write path after Lanre's feedback, fixed a copy bug where the shared ManagerPinField hardcoded 'reversal' wording onto the count screen, and pulled the posting half of reversal into one shared function because reversing line-by-line would have re-run bcrypt once per line and blown the statement timeout on a large count. Frontend still uncommitted. 041 closed three review findings: the mid-count double count (warn with PT449, name up to five items, confirm with the same idempotency key — never silently subtract, because the system cannot know whether the counter saw the delivery), an ELSE false on the state-shape CHECK which was failing open, and the anon quarantine array replaced by one shared assert_no_anon_security_definer() that future migrations call in one line. 038/039/040 keep their own copies deliberately: editing an applied migration makes the record a lie. DEPLOYED 16 Aug: merged to main at 596cb9e, Vercel building, database and frontend level again. Final tally 178 SQL assertions across three dry runs (each applying its migration twice in one transaction and rolling back), 46 post-push checks against the remote, 36 render assertions. Not yet clicked through by a human — that is batched into 1.1i.

shipments.t: Complete the item record: selling price, valuation, photo

Landing page shows value at cost (moving average) and retail value side by side, plus margin, each labelled so the two can never be confused
Item photo at tenant level, reusing the existing media_assets pipeline rather than growing a second one
Searchable typeahead pickers for location and item, filtered server-side against the same query the list uses, because a hotel with 1,000 items cannot scroll a dropdown
shipments.proof: An Ingredient row with a price is rejected and a Sold as-is row without one is rejected. Cost value and retail value each reconcile to a hand-written query. A photo survives a reload and lands nowhere publicly readable that it should not.
shipments.note: 042 PUSHED and verified live; frontend not yet committed. Price is NET of tax, deliberately: 021 adds tax on top of a charge's net_amount, and a tax-inclusive price would have overstated margin by a different amount at every property — silently, with nothing erroring. The sellable-must-be-priced half is a TRIGGER not a CHECK, because adding a constraint validates existing rows and the live database already had an unpriced sellable item; the gap is made findable by a filter instead of blocked by an invented price. Item images go tenant-level through the existing media_assets path — and needed a plain tenant FK beside the composite one, because a composite FK is MATCH SIMPLE and skips checking entirely once property_id is null. Nine pickers converted, not the four the brief named. CLOSED 19 Aug: figures confirmed live — 6 positions, 5 excluded for having no price, cost ₦533,000, retail ₦168,000 (Coke alone, 240 x ₦700), margin ₦60,000 subtracting only Coke's cost rather than the whole shelf.

ships: Lightweight receipt into the store: date, item, quantity in base units, unit cost, supplier as free text
Manager-permissioned direct receipt elsewhere, mandatory reason, flagged
Write-off as its own movement type with reasons: spoilage, breakage, expiry, staff meal, complimentary

shipments.proof: Receive at a higher price and watch the moving average move by the exact weighted amount. Write off a unit and confirm it reads as recorded loss, not as unexplained variance.
shipments.note: Closes the gap between go-live and stage 7 purchasing. Without it the average cost freezes at opening and every valuation drifts. Stage 7 later upgrades this into receive-against-order without changing the movement. DEPLOYED 21 Aug (migration 043 applied first, then code — the safe direction). 56 SQL assertions, 310 render assertions across 9 proofs. Three things the proofs found that the reasoning had wrong: the late-openings view keyed on created_at could never have fired, because created_at defaults to now() which is TRANSACTION start time, so rows written together tie to the microsecond — it uses seq instead, the column 036 created for exactly this; a second `|| true` tautology assertion; and a deliberate wrong-average breakage that stayed GREEN because the assertion recomputed from its own constants instead of calling the component. The receive test is kind='store', not is_default_store, so a hotel's second store receives without ceremony.

shipments.t: A write-off we cannot value says so first
ships: A second overridable gate on post_stock_writeoff, fired when the movement would carry NO cost basis at all -- never when the basis is zero, which is a value
The same gate on post_stock_adjustment, on the way out only; a positive adjustment states its own cost and trips neither
Its own errcode, PT450, so the client can tell it from the negative-stock PT449 and offer the right confirm step -- two questions, never merged into one "are you sure"
The message in the database with a hint naming the three ways out: record the opening balance first, date it on or after the first receipt, or confirm writing it off unvalued
ConfirmGatePanel, one component for both screens, so the two moments read alike and cannot drift apart
The answers CARRY FORWARD: a movement can trip both gates in turn, and confirming the second does not drop the first
The staff guide gains "When the system does not know what the stock cost", with the worked back-dated case and the three ways out
shipments.proof: 050's self-verify: 13 assertions, five breakages, each turning exactly the named one red -- removing the gates, testing the basis for = 0 instead of IS NULL, ignoring the override, leaving the adjustment ungated (the likeliest half-done shipment), and letting finish_stock_take acquire the gate. The render proof drives the real ConfirmGatePanel: 12 assertions on two fixtures that disagree on every word, so a panel printing one sentence for both gates goes red whichever one it picks. Three breakages there, all red. The confirmed write-off and 048's bucket are ONE fixture, so the question and its consequence are one test.
shipments.note: THE GAP, between two guards that ask different questions. The negative guard asks WHAT IS ON HAND TODAY; the cost basis asks WHAT THE AVERAGE WAS AS AT THE MOVEMENT'S DATE. Write off 4 kg dated 1 October against a position holding 10 kg received on 5 October: on-hand-today is 10, the result is 6, no guard fires -- and the as-at average is undefined, so the movement leaves the shelf carrying nothing and nobody is told. Writing off from an EMPTY shelf was already gated by PT449; the back-dated case sailed straight through. 048 measured the cost of it at -4,000.00 on a fixture. NOT A REFUSAL, deliberately. Section 9 holds: blocking teaches staff to invent fake receipts, and a write-off is a storekeeper ADMITTING a loss -- refuse the admission and you get an invisible loss or fabricated purchase data, in the system built to catch theft. What changes is that recording it becomes deliberate. THE GATE CANNOT DISAGREE WITH THE TRIGGER, because it calls the same function rather than reimplementing the fold. 038 stamps carried_unit_cost from stock_average_cost_as_at with the row's own seq; the gate passes NULL, which that function documents as "after everything". They agree exactly because seq is table-wide and the new row's is larger than every existing one. FOUND BY THIS SHIPMENT'S OWN FIXTURE FAILING, and recorded in the migration header rather than quietly fixed: the gate asks ONCE PER POSITION PER DATE, not once per movement. After the first unvaluable movement on a date, the fold has a row to walk and returns an average of ZERO rather than NULL for later movements that day -- measured, 0.0000 against NULL one day earlier. The second movement genuinely will carry a basis of zero, and zero is a value. The consequence worth knowing is that only the first lands in 048's unvaluable bucket; the rest show up in valuation_difference. Defensible as a GATE, because the alternative is the gate and the trigger disagreeing about what a basis is -- so the gate still asks once. What was NOT left alone is the REPORT: 051 redefines 048's bucket as a fact about a POSITION rather than about a movement, so every movement off a position with no basis is named, not just the first. The screen's sentence was already written per-position ("N movements left a position that had no cost history"), which 048 made aspirational and 051 makes true. finish_stock_take IS NOT GATED AND MUST NOT BE. A count adjustment downward on a position with no cost history is the same case, and refusing it at the end of an hour's walking is brutal and teaches people to fudge the count. The architecture already enforces it -- finish_stock_take inserts its movements directly rather than calling post_stock_adjustment -- and 050's self-verify asserts on pg_get_functiondef that it has not acquired the gate on purpose either, so "completing" it later fails the migration. NO NEW COLUMN RECORDS THE ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: carried_unit_cost being NULL IS the record, and 048 already reports it by value. A second record of one fact is a second thing to keep in step.

shipments.t: The books: accounts, mappings and the journal
ships: Chart of accounts, seeded for a new tenant the same way categories and units already are, editable
Account mappings by role key, 27 keys derived from every place money moves in the code today, not from purchasing
A property can override a mapping; without one the group default applies. Two hotels, two tills, one chart
Journal entries numbered JE-000001, permanent, never updated, never deleted, reversed only by counter-entry
One post_journal function: refuses an unbalanced entry, honours the posting lock, posts once per source document
One rounding line, capped at a naira, because weighted-average cost carries four decimals and the books carry two. Nothing else may absorb a difference
A missing mapping refuses the posting and names the role key. No suspense account for errors to hide in
A settings screen showing role key to account, and when something last posted to it, so a missing wiring is visible rather than remembered
Choosing the account becomes part of creating a charge category, so the failure can never reach the front desk
gl_start_date per property: the posting lock refuses the document, this lets the document through and books no entry
shipments.proof: Applied to the remote first, then verified directly rather than trusting the exit code: 35 accounts, 31 mappings, 0 charge categories missing a role key, 0 journal entries because nothing is wired yet, RLS on every table, and assert_no_anon_security_definer() passing on the live database. The first real entry posts at 1.1h2, and that is where the end-to-end proof lives.
shipments.note: Built now, not in stage 11, and that is a reversal. Accounting was placed last on the argument that a ledger built for one module fits one module. The counter-argument is timing: Heledon has not gone live, so there is no trading history to backfill, and every module that posts nothing today becomes history somebody reconstructs later. The folio has been charging and taking payments since 021 with nowhere to post, and that debt should not survive go-live. The scope is deliberately the spine only: somewhere for money to go, not something to read. Trial balance, P&L, balance sheet, reconciliation and tax returns all stay in stage 11, where they become reports over a ledger that was correct from the first entry. The role keys are derived from every posting site in the code today rather than from purchasing, so the spine is wired against all of it once. Wiring order after Code's §0: the spine is designed against the folio, the stock ledger and purchasing at once, then wired progressively. The six stock RPCs that already move money post from 1.1h2, alongside purchasing, so the ledger's inventory balance and the stock valuation can never disagree. The folio follows at 1.1h4. That gap is dated in the migration header rather than left as an exception nobody wrote down. DEPLOYED 23 Aug, commit be8584a, migration applied before the code as always: migration 044, 1,759 lines, 51 SQL assertions with 11 guards removed one at a time and all 11 going red, 343 render assertions across 10 proofs. 35 accounts and 31 mappings seeded, four accounts deliberately unmapped. Two proofs earned their keep: the idempotency guard needed both the lookup and the unique index removed before it went red, because either one masks the other on a single connection, so the index is asserted structurally instead; and a breakage turned two row assertions red while the headline total stayed green, the same lesson 1.1g taught from the other direction, that a total is the assertion most likely to be mistaken for coverage. Code added a guard nobody asked for and should have: the GL start date cannot move once the books have opened. The two debts from the pre-push questions are recorded in 044's header and in the wiring table in ARCHITECTURE.md, which is where someone already looks for what wires when. gl_start_date is deliberately null on Heledon: it gets set once, at go-live.

shipments.t: The chart of accounts, as an accountant expects to see it
ships: The accounts themselves, listed and grouped in financial-statement order: assets, liabilities, equity, revenue, expenses
Dense table, one line per account, codes right-aligned in tabular numerals. A spreadsheet, not a settings form
Add an account, which a hotel with three bank accounts needs on day one
The code is suggested as the next free number in that group's range, so nobody has to know that a liability starts with 2
An account that has been posted to can be renamed but never renumbered and never deleted. Deactivate instead, and not while a mapping still points at it
Search across code and name
Where money posts becomes the second tab, same density, keeping the role key to account mapping that shipped with the spine
Accounts ordered by their own code within each section, so an added account lands where its number says it belongs rather than at the top of the chart
An account that has been posted to cannot change its group either. Moving one from asset to expense would silently restate a balance sheet somebody has already read
shipments.proof: Applied to the remote first, then verified: display_order dropped, the index rebuilt on the code, all four change rules live on the trigger, 35 accounts reading asset to liability to equity to revenue to expense. 24 SQL assertions with 6 guards red when removed, 55 render assertions with 5 breakages. The ordering gate runs against a deliberately shuffled fixture, so a sort that did nothing would fail it.
shipments.note: Lanre looked at the Accounts tab on live and said it does not read like accounting. He was right, and the gap was mine: I specified a mapping screen and called it the accounts screen. Two different objects. The chart of accounts is the list an auditor is handed and a trial balance is that same list with balances on it, so it cannot wait for stage 11. A hotel could not see its own accounts or add one. Code's read-only pass found the defect that would have shipped: display_order defaults to 0, so the first account a hotel added would have sorted above Cash and looked like a broken screen. Fixed by removing the dependency rather than the default, ordering on the code itself. Group headers and a non-postable flag were dropped after the same pass showed there is no parent column for a header to head and no manual journal screen to protect an account from; that flag is recorded as owed when stage 11 gives someone a way to post by hand. DEPLOYED 24 Aug, commit 5b3b8a3. The sticky header did not work as specified and Code measured rather than guessed: inside the standard table wrapper the header sat 233 pixels off the top of the screen, because a horizontal overflow container is also a vertical one with no height to scroll. The working pattern is extracted with both failure modes written into it, including why sticky must sit on the header cell and never the row, a defect invisible in the browser you build in. Rule 27 went into CLAUDE.md from three sightings in three shipments: an assertion that cannot tell working from absent is not an assertion, so name the defect that turns it red before trusting a green run.

shipments.t: Purchases: suppliers, the order, and receiving it
ships: Suppliers as real records, one name only: a partial unique index on the lowercased name stops the same supplier existing twice
Suppliers carry what paying them will need: tax ID, withholding rate, bank details. Captured now because a column added to an empty table is free and a backfill conversation with a live hotel is not
Purchase order as the document, numbered PO-000001 from the counter that already exists
Four statuses: draft, ordered, received, cancelled. 'In transit' is a label the screen derives from outstanding lines, so it can never disagree with the data
An ordered purchase order is immutable. Reality is recorded against it, never written over it
Destination on every line (inventory, asset, expense) legal from day one; only inventory can be received in this shipment
Receive on the order itself, same page. Quantity per line, difference against ordered shown live, a reason required before a difference will post
Over-receipt allowed on a manager PIN rather than refused, so nobody has to invent numbers
Cost difference between what was agreed and what the invoice says, shown live and stored, without a mandatory box people learn to type through
One transaction inside the RPC: receipt, receipt lines and stock movements commit together or not at all
Supplier activity derived from the documents. No stored balance column, and not called an account until payments give it a second side
Quantity field accepts 10*24 and stores 240. Base units only, no conversion factor anywhere
Every receipt posts its own journal through the spine, inside the same transaction. No client-side posting, no backfill page
The six stock RPCs that already move money post too: opening, adjustment, receipt, write-off, count variance and reversal. Inventory in the books and inventory in the ledger cannot disagree
Purchases and Suppliers side by side in the sidebar, filling the slot already sitting there marked soon

The check the ERP could never make: the ledger's inventory balance against an independent recomputation from the movements themselves, on its own Accounts tab, with the rounding residue against the stock valuation shown rather than hidden
A list of any movement carrying no journal entry, with the reason. An empty reason is the alarm

A dated alarm rather than a silenced one: movements written before this property's RPCs began posting carry a recorded reason, so the list reads zero on day one and still fires on a movement written after the wiring with no entry
The rounding residue shown beside the number of movements it accumulated over, and every position that has ever been below zero named on the card with the sentence that explains it
shipments.proof: Order 50kg of rice, receive 47kg: the shortfall demands a reason, the ledger moves by exactly 47, the movement names the goods-received note, and re-sending the same request with a changed quantity is refused rather than silently ignored. Kill the transaction halfway and confirm none of it happened. 77 database assertions on a throwaway property inside the transaction, re-run against seven deliberately broken versions of the migration, plus 63 render assertions with five mutations. 048 then closed the one defect that kept this open: 4 assertions on a fixture that rolls itself back by aborting a subtransaction, run against four deliberate breakages of which three go red and the fourth is documented as uncatchable by this fixture, plus 84 render assertions with three mutations of the card's own sentence. Applied to live on 2 November; the reconciliation reads 0.00 on every figure.
shipments.note: Modelled on how purchasing actually runs in Palstro ERP after a read-only investigation of that codebase, then corrected where the ERP's own migration history showed the scars: three overloaded status columns that 068 had to arbitrate; no destination field at all; journals posted client-side after the RPC returned, leaving the GL 50,000 adrift from the subledger until 067 repaired it; a receive screen with no quantity input despite a schema that supports one; two near-identical received-quantity columns; receipt numbers from count(*)+1, which races; and a supplier balance column the code itself does not trust. Two decisions changed after Code's read-only §0. Purchasing was going to post no journals, because the hotel schema has no ledger at all. Lanre overruled that and he was right: Heledon has not gone live, so this is the last moment when wiring the books costs one shipment instead of a reconstruction project. The spine lands first as 1.1h and this shipment posts into it from its first line. And goods in transit is a state of the order rather than a real location, because landing stock out of a transit location needs the transfer RPCs that do not exist until 6.1, and because teaching post_stock_receipt that one non-store location is secretly fine is how a guard rots. Nothing built in 1.1g is wasted: purchasing calls the same receipt RPC, extended additively so a movement can name the order it came from, and direct receipt survives as the cash-and-carry exception. Two corrections came out of the build, both mine. The reconciliation I specified, that the inventory account equals the stock valuation to the kobo, is not always true and should not be: the ledger sums per-movement values each rounded to the kobo while the valuation carries an average at full precision, so 3 at 10.00 plus 1 at 11.11 legitimately disagree by a kobo. Asserting the ledger against an independent recomputation from the movements is both true and stronger. And one deliberate breakage stayed green because the fixture made the right and the wrong answer the same number, valuing a reversal at an average that had not moved since. That is rule 27 from a fourth direction and it now carries a corollary: a fixture where the correct and incorrect computations coincide cannot test either one. 047 followed within the day because the first look at live showed both reconciliation surfaces lying: the alarm list read 8 rather than 0, and the difference read 533,000 out, because Heledon holds build-era movements written before anything posted. Fixed with a recorded fact, gl_wired_at, not a tolerance: code that did not exist cannot have posted. Two fudges were rejected by name in the migration header, ignoring anything older than N days, and borrowing gl_start_date to silence it. 046 also asked the wrong question about negative positions, counting the ones below zero today rather than the ones that have ever been below zero, which are the only ones that explain a divergence and are usually positive again by the time anyone looks. Three checks were raised against 047 afterwards. Two came back clean, and the second of those was retracted after being tested rather than argued: two views that read exactly like a cross-tenant leak turn out to scope themselves in their own WHERE. The third was a real defect and 048 closed it: a movement with no cost basis is NOT absent from the valuation, so a back-dated write-off threw the reconciliation out by the value of the stock written off, and 047's own comment claimed the opposite. Measured at minus 4,000 on a fixture. The fix is a bucket rather than a reworded comment, because the reconciliation already names every other category of value that legitimately never reached the ledger and absorbs none of them: unvaluable_value is computed from the movements, reported on the card in words an owner can act on, and the headline figure returns to zero when that is the only cause. 047's claim is replaced rather than softened. Building that proof taught the sharpest lesson of the shipment: the first two fixtures were green against a PLUG, a bucket defined as the very difference it was meant to explain, which is true by construction and can never be wrong. It took a third fixture carrying genuine rounding beside the unvaluable movement to put the honest computation and the plug on different numbers, 4,000.00 against 3,999.99. One further breakage is recorded as still green rather than hidden: dropping the per-position round() cannot be caught until a property holds several fractional unvaluable positions. Nothing was ever wrong on live, because no such movement exists yet.

ships: A reversal of the RECEIPT, as a document — not a stock movement reversed from the item ledger with the paperwork left behind it
The counter movement and the counter journal entry posted in the same transaction as the reversal, so the three stores cannot end up disagreeing (rule 7)
A mandatory reason and a manager PIN, recorded against the manager by name, the same shape as every other undoing in this product
Every purchasing read excluding what has been reversed: received_quantity, outstanding_quantity, is_settled, received_value, the supplier activity row, and stock_over_receipts
The reversed delivery still VISIBLE on the order, marked as reversed with its reason — a delivery that happened and was undone is two facts, not zero

purchase_order_settled_status(): the status derivation extracted so receive, the reversal and the transition trigger share one definition — and the trigger uses it to VALIDATE a walk-back rather than trust the caller
p_post_journal on post_movement_reversal, so a delivery's reversal posts ONE mirror entry instead of one per movement
reverse_stock_movement refuses a movement that arrived on a delivery, and the receipt trigger's hint stops recommending the half-measure it used to be the only alternative to
shipments.proof: Live, rolled back: an order of two lines delivered in two goes reads received; reverse one delivery and it reads part_received; reverse the other and it reads ordered, with the position back to where it started and the counter carrying the basis it unwinds rather than the average, which the fixture first moves off 100 so the two cannot coincide. Four journal entries net to zero on every account. An over-received delivery leaves stock_over_receipts and stays on the delivery history with its authorising manager. Reversing the first of two deliveries of 6 against 10 leaves nothing reading as over-received.
shipments.note: MEASURED, NOT INFERRED. A receipt is permanent by trigger (046 forbid_purchase_receipt_change refuses every UPDATE and DELETE on purchase_receipts and their lines) and cancel_purchase_order refuses outright on a received order, so the only correction that exists today is post_movement_reversal from the item ledger — which writes a NEW stock_movements row and touches no purchasing record. Dry-run against the live GRN-000002 inside a rolled-back transaction: on-hand oil in Main Store went 25.0000 to 0.0000, and stock_over_receipts still reported it over by 5.0000 while purchase_order_summary still read 200,000.00 received. THE GAP IS THE MODULE'S, NOT THE VIEW'S. Every purchasing read is built on purchase_receipt_lines, which nothing links a reversal to, so received_quantity, outstanding_quantity, is_settled, received_value, the supplier row and stock_over_receipts all ignore reversals identically. 049 inherited that behaviour rather than adding a hole; what it added is the first screen that puts the consequence in front of an owner with a manager's name against it, which is what makes it worth deciding now. Reversing the movement and leaving the receipt saying the goods arrived is two records disagreeing about one event, which is the thing this module exists to prevent. SEQUENCING: IT LANDED BEFORE 1.1h5. A supplier payment is allocated against what a delivery says arrived, so a receipt that cannot be undone correctly becomes money paid for goods that went back. MOVED FROM later TO next ON 4 NOVEMBER, and the reason is 1.1h3 rather than 1.1h5. 052 shipped expenses and fixed_assets with no void column at all, deliberately -- a column nothing can write is a promise the next person has to keep -- so undoing the delivery is now the ONLY correction path a mis-received asset or expense has. A freezer received against the wrong order is permanent until this ships. It still lands before 1.1h5 for the original reason; it now lands before anything else, because every receive enabled without it is another record nobody can correct. SHIPPED AS 056 AND 057. THE PART THAT NEEDED A DECISION WAS THE ORDER STATUS, not the reversal: 046 treated received as terminal, so reversing the receipt that settled an order would have left it reading received with nothing received — measured first, all three walk-backs refused PT409 with a hint saying "This order is complete." The thing that decided the fix is that the status was ALREADY derived: receive computed it from the rows and said so in its own comment, so v_unsettled was extracted into purchase_order_settled_status() and the walk-back edges made legal ONLY when the new status equals what the lines say. The trigger checks the claim rather than the caller, so no RPC — including the one that reverses — can set a status the deliveries do not support. Rejected by name: widening the transition table unconditionally, and gating it on a session signal the trigger trusts, which answers who is calling instead of whether it is true. The extraction turned up a latent defect in the FORWARD path that nothing else in the shipment would have caught: v_unsettled did not exclude reversed receipts, so receiving again after a reversal would have counted the reversed delivery. THE LEDGER IS A MIRROR, NOT A RECOMPUTATION. post_movement_reversal gained p_post_journal because a delivery posts one entry for the whole receipt and so must its reversal — same accounts, same amounts, sides flipped. A mirror nets to zero per account by construction; a recomputation nets to zero only if the rounding agrees, and 046 already learned those can legitimately differ by a kobo. The flag carries its own warning rather than a shipment note: passing false without posting an entry leaves the ledger short by the value of the stock with nothing to show it. NO VOID COLUMN WAS ADDED to expenses or fixed_assets. Each row anchors on a receipt line, so reversed is a join rather than a third writable promise on two tables that just had two taken off them — which keeps 052's header true as written. Two hints in the database's own voice were rewritten in the same file as the thing that made them wrong, because a database telling somebody to do the wrong thing is worse than one that says nothing: the receipt trigger said to reverse the stock movement, and reverse_stock_movement would have gone on doing it. FOUR OF THE TWENTY-FOUR BREAKAGES FOUND DEFECTS IN THE ASSERTIONS RATHER THAN THE CODE, and two were green while the thing they existed to catch was happening. 056's entry count and netting were scoped to the two receipts, so they could not see an entry sourced on a MOVEMENT — the stock half of the ledger reversed TWICE stayed green at 11 of 11. 057's supplier_activity check compared against the summary only after the reversal, where the right answer is 0.00 and a view hardcoding 0 agrees perfectly. Both now straddle the boundary where the right and wrong answers are different numbers. One render-proof assertion also went red against correct code, which is the expensive direction: it asserted a non-stock delivery does not say "goes back out", and the non-stock sentence reads "nothing goes back out of a store". NOT IN THIS SHIPMENT AND NAMED IN 056'S HEADER: 1.1h5 owns both directions of the payment rule — refusing to reverse a receipt a payment is allocated to, and refusing to allocate a payment to a receipt that was reversed.

shipments.t: Where else a purchase can go: assets and expenses
ships: One expenses table from the start, with a nullable link to the purchase line, so a purchase expense and a standalone expense are never two places to look
Fixed asset records carrying the supplier and the order that bought them
Category lists modelled on charge_categories: a stable machine code apart from the display name
The receive RPC accepts all three destinations
Six seeded expense accounts 5300-5350 with their mappings, so a category resolves through account_mappings and never a hardcoded code
line_type denormalised onto the receipt line with a composite FK, so a receipt line whose type differs from its order line's cannot exist
expense_category_id on the order line, chosen when the order is RAISED rather than at the door, because the person raising it knows a call-out is a repair
The manager gate narrowed to deliveries that actually move stock: a freezer going to the bar no longer demands a PIN the server then refuses as unnecessary
A Kind selector on every order line, with a description field and a server-searched category typeahead behind it
The delivery history names an asset or an expense instead of the em-dash it showed where item_name is null
shipments.proof: Migrations 052-055: 17 + 9 + 4 + 3 assertions, 9 + 8 + 4 + 4 breakages all red. Render proof PART 7 (purchasing) made to fail ten ways, and popover PART 7 three. Live: rice, a freezer and a plumber's call-out on one order, received once -- stock moved, the register gained the freezer with its supplier, the call-out debited repairs, and one entry credited the supplier with the sum of three debits.
shipments.note: Split out of 1.1h because neither an expenses nor a fixed assets table exists in the schema today, so the destination rule means building two record tables. Records, not modules: no depreciation and no approval flow, those are 8.5 and 7.1. The ERP keeps assets and expenses outside purchasing entirely, which is why a vendor view there has to union three places. SHIPPED WITH TWO COLUMNS DELIBERATELY ABSENT: expenses carried is_voided and fixed_assets carried deleted_at, and neither could ever have been set -- no update policy by design and no definer function to void either -- so the comment beside them promised a way back that did not exist. Both dropped, and assertion 7 now refuses a soft-delete column that has no policy or RPC able to write it. The correction path today is to undo the delivery (1.1h2d); standalone entry ships with its own void path and the column returns then. 052's first draft also had NO RLS on three new tables and nothing failed, because nothing asked; assertion 6 reads relrowsecurity now. Two defects found outside the brief and fixed: the popover primitive placed its panel once and never again, so a typeahead whose rows arrive later grew 171px past the bottom of a phone screen with two options unreachable -- it affected every picker since 1.1e -- and the manager gate was wider than the rule it enforced.

shipments.t: The folio wired into the books
ships: LANDED (058): tax captured on the charge at post time, before anything is wired. It was computed live from the current rate, so changing VAT silently rewrote every past bill — the same defect booking_nights was built to prevent

LANDED (059): the REVENUE ACCOUNT captured on the charge too. charge_categories.account_role_key has an admin UPDATE policy, so a charge posted under one account and reversed after a repoint credited one and debited another: both entries balancing, neither ever clearing. 058's defect one column over

LANDED (059): a tax carries its OWN account instead of one inferred from applies_to, and 058's captured rows carry it. A state consumption tax is also 'taxable' and would have landed in the VAT account, reconciling perfectly while owing money to the wrong authority

LANDED (059): gl_wired_at split into stock_gl_wired_at and folio_gl_wired_at. One timestamp cannot explain two modules' pre-wiring gaps, and a charge posted between the two wirings is explained by neither

LANDED (059): 'other' off the payment picker. It has no account and must not have one (044: a missing mapping is a loud failure, never a suspense account), so it would have refused at the counter with a guest standing there. Zero payments carried it

LANDED (061): a charge's entry is struck on GROSS and DISCOUNT as separate legs, never on net. On net, a discounted charge and its reversal leave equal residues in revenue and discounts_allowed that balance, reconcile and never clear; it also hides how much was given away

LANDED (062): CHARGES POST. post_charge and post_charge_reversal each call the helper at the end, after their own tax step — posting before it gives an entry with NO TAX LEGS that still BALANCES, because the receivable is the open line, so the bill posts short by the whole VAT with nothing erroring and post_journal's uniqueness makes it permanent. Not on any of the three early-return paths: a redelivered key must not mint an entry for a pre-wiring document

LANDED (062, no code): ONE ENTRY PER NIGHT. booking_nights has no folio link — a night reaches the bill as its own folio_charges row via post_room_night_charge — so one charge is one entry and item 3 was a proof, not a build. Found by counting the call sites, of which the whole folio module has four

LANDED (062): THE FOLIO PRODUCES FUTURE-DATED DOCUMENTS AND post_journal REFUSES THEM. Found by wiring it: check_out_booking bills the FULL reserved range, so a guest leaving early is billed for nights still ahead, and naive wiring made checkout fail outright with PT422 — 026's own scenario. The helper now DECLINES a document whose day has not come (null, 046's precedent) because revenue for the 7th belongs to the 7th, and post_charge REFUSES a forward date it was not given (p_allow_future, passed only by post_room_night_charge), because a bar charge dated next week is a typo and nothing refused it before

LANDED (062): folio_gl_wired_at stamped, and the six pre-wiring documents left unposted — as 047 did on the stock side rather than invent entries for documents written before the code. Backfilling is worse here: two discount applications have moved the laundry charge's net since it was posted, so reconstructing its entry means deciding what it looked like at a moment nobody recorded

LANDED (063): DISCOUNTS AND PAYMENTS POST. apply_charge_discount posts the DELTA keyed on the application row (060), skipping a zero delta because post_journal RAISES on a zero balancing line — so without the skip a manager re-approving the same amount would be refused. record_payment posts the money side at the account its METHOD maps to, by an explicit whitelist that refuses an unknown method BY NAME

LANDED (063): the same forward-date question on both paths, answered OPPOSITELY. A discount on a night that has not arrived is dated to that night (060), so the helper DECLINES — a manager reducing a forward night must not be told the ledger refused. A PAYMENT dated forward was accepted with no guard at all, and there is no caller for whom it is real: money is not received tomorrow, so record_payment REFUSES with no escape parameter

LANDED (063): a payment by method 'other' is now refused outright rather than written as a row the ledger can never accept. 044 settled that a missing mapping is a loud failure and never a suspense account; 059 took it off the picker. Nothing offers it, zero rows carry it, and the constraint still allows it so history stays representable
Food and drink charges and service charge post through the spine as ordinary charges (062)

LANDED (061, as a consequence): the night audit posts ONE ENTRY PER NIGHT without a line of code for it, because booking_nights has no folio link — a night reaches the bill as its own folio_charges row via post_room_night_charge, so one charge is one entry. Found by counting the call sites rather than by reasoning about the modules, which would have produced a fourth helper nobody needed. At the grain run_night_audit already keys on, never one per run. An entry covering several nights cannot be idempotent against a half-run audit, and a half-run night audit is not a hypothetical

LANDED (060): a discount is an EVENT, not a column. folio_charge_discounts holds one insert-only row per application of apply_charge_discount — previous amount, new amount, a GENERATED signed delta, its own approver, its own idempotency key, and a seq for real insertion order. The four discount_* columns stay as current state so no reader changes

LANDED (060): the live retry defect it exposed. The idempotency check read ONE mutable column, so it could only recognise the newest key; a redelivered earlier key looked new and re-applied itself — measured on the live schema, an 800 discount went back to 500, the tax from 699.20 to 722.00, and the later manager's reason was overwritten. Nothing errored. A replay also now refuses a key that belongs to a DIFFERENT charge, naming both: keys are unique per tenant, so the lookup found a real application and handed that other charge back as a success

LANDED (061): a discount posts the DELTA, keyed on the folio_charge_discounts row rather than the charge. Keying on the charge posts once: journal_entries is unique on (tenant, source type, source id), so the second application is handed the first entry back and its delta never reaches the books. The TAX delta moves with it, computed per tax ACCOUNT as round((gross - new) * rate) - round((gross - previous) * rate) — every input a captured fact, the same expression restate_charge_taxes uses

LANDED (061): a zero-delta application is SKIPPED by the helper, not absorbed. The same amount re-approved with a different reason is a real event and is kept; post_journal RAISES on a balancing line of zero rather than ignoring it

LANDED (061): the three posting helpers, in 046's pattern — post_folio_charge_journal, post_folio_discount_journal, post_folio_payment_journal. NOTHING CALLS THEM YET: post_charge, post_charge_reversal, apply_charge_discount and record_payment are byte-for-byte untouched, so no front-desk action behaves differently. The whole folio module wires at FOUR call sites, because only two functions insert into folio_charges and only one into folio_payments — and there are FIVE document types, not three, since void_charge and void_payment write no row and so need one of their own

LANDED (061): the guest ledger leg IS THE RESIDUAL, so a zero residual gets no leg. Measured by building one: comp a charge 100% and reverse it, and the counter arrives net 0 with its tax restated to 0, so an unconditional open line works out at zero and post_journal raises. Unconditional, reversing a comped charge would fail outright at the desk

LANDED (061): the payment method mapped by an explicit whitelist that REFUSES BY NAME. A role key built by concatenation fails as a missing account_mappings row, which somebody fixes by adding a mapping — when the real answer is that a method nobody decided an account for has reached the front desk. 'other' is the one legal value with no account, and it is what the assertion exercises

LANDED (067): A REFUND IS ITS OWN ACT, and finding that out was the whole of item 9. record_payment refused only a ZERO amount, so a NEGATIVE one was ordinary business: measured as an ordinary member of the tenant, record_payment(folio, -50000, 'cash', ...) was ACCEPTED, credited cash 50,000.00 and debited the guest ledger 50,000.00. Fifty thousand naira of cash out of the till with no approval and no reason — while the SAME movement through reverse_payment is refused with 'Reversing a payment always requires a valid manager PIN'. One act, two routes, opposite controls

LANDED (067): and the screen was pointing at the unguarded one. TakePaymentForm's help text read 'Enter a negative amount to record a refund', so the desk was being instructed to use it. Set against the module, a refund sat below the bar a VOID clears: a void takes a reason (021), a reversal takes a reason and a PIN (031), a refund took NEITHER — while being the only one of the three where cash physically leaves the building

LANDED (067): record_refund, named so rather than refund_payment, because 'refund a payment' implies an argument it does not have — it takes a FOLIO. A REASON and a MANAGER PIN mandatory BY SIGNATURE rather than by a branch, and the replay lookup deliberately BEFORE the PIN so a retried payout does not fetch the manager back to a terminal whose drawer is already open (060, 065). The row is written THROUGH record_payment, so the method whitelist, the folio-status rule, the business date, the idempotency handling and the posting call stay in one place and a refund cannot drift from a payment in any of them

LANDED (067): AND A CEILING, which is the part that is more than an approval. A refund cannot exceed what that folio has actually received, refused BY NAME with both figures and a hint saying what it is instead: paying out more than came in is a petty cash payment (4.3), not a refund. The figure is READ from folio_totals.payments_total — the NET, so the ceiling falls as refunds are taken and a fully-refunded folio refuses the next at zero. Asserted on BOTH sides of the boundary, and on the difference between the net and the sum of payments IN, which are the same number until the first refund lands

LANDED (067): record_payment now does ONE DIRECTION and refuses the other by name (PT405), with p_allow_negative for its two entitled callers — reverse_payment and record_refund. 052's ruling and 062's: refuse at the moment of the decision, not of the consequence. And the flag is NOT the control, proven rather than claimed: a bare p_allow_negative gets past the function and is then refused by the TABLE, because folio_payments carries a deferred constraint trigger requiring every money-out row to be either a reversal counter or an approved refund

LANDED (067): a DEFERRED constraint trigger rather than a CHECK, and the reason is not style. A refund is completed by the statement AFTER its insert, and a CHECK fires per statement and cannot be deferred — the alternatives were record_refund duplicating five of record_payment's rules, or record_payment taking approved_by as a parameter, which would let a PostgREST caller name any manager with no PIN. It also RE-READS the row instead of trusting the trigger's NEW, which a deferred AFTER trigger is handed as it was at the triggering statement: written the other way it refused 067's own refunds

LANDED (067, no code): THE DEPOSIT HALF WAS ALREADY DECIDED AGAINST, IN WRITING. Money held for a stay that has not begun is strictly a LIABILITY, and this line used to promise that treatment — but 044 §7.2 says 'THERE IS NO guest_deposits KEY, AND THAT IS A DECISION RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT ... It becomes worth doing the day somebody needs deposits held separately on a balance sheet, which is stage 11 at the earliest.' So the promise was corrected rather than kept, the split sits on 11.4 where its own trigger fires, and assertion 15 proves the deposit still posts as it did: cash Dr 50,000, guest_ledger Cr 50,000, folio balance -50,000, and 066 reconciles it at exactly zero

LANDED (067, NOT done): void_payment still has no manager PIN, and that is said out loud rather than quietly left. Voiding a received payment also erases recorded money; it takes a reason but no approval, 021 §9.5 reasons that explicitly ('a serious act and is fully logged'), and 064 now posts its counter-entry too. A different control, deliberately chosen. If it needs revisiting it gets its own conversation rather than a ride on this one

LANDED (067): 17 breakages, 16 red. The one GREEN is a finding: deleting the grant line changed nothing, because THIS PROJECT'S DEFAULT PRIVILEGES already grant EXECUTE on every new function to anon, authenticated and service_role. So a grant line is belt-and-braces and the REVOKE FROM ANON is the load-bearing one — a new function is reachable by an unauthenticated caller until revoked, which is now asserted on the trigger function rather than assumed

LANDED (065): EVERY REVERSAL PATH RECONCILES, proven end to end through the CLIENT-CALLABLE RPCs rather than the internal writers. reverse_charge, reverse_discount, reverse_payment, reverse_no_show, void_charge and void_payment all net to zero; reverse_checkout and reverse_cancel are asserted as 'the folio still reconciles' rather than 'they post nothing', because the day a fee is added posting becomes the CORRECT behaviour and a proof that fails for doing the right thing gets deleted rather than understood

LANDED (065): and the proof found one more defect. A PAYMENT REVERSAL'S ENTRY DID NOT KNOW WHAT IT UNWOUND. post_charge_reversal sets its link in the INSERT, so a charge counter was always linked; reverse_payment sets it in a SEPARATE statement after record_payment — which from 063 posted inside exactly that gap, so reverses_entry_id was silently NULL. Every amount was right and only the audit pointer was gone. Fixed with 046's own p_post_journal shape: record_payment is told not to post, the link is written, then reverse_payment posts

LANDED (065): 031's comment on that statement — 'same transaction, so no window exists in which the counter-payment is unlinked' — is rule 28's THIRD instance. True of the folio tables, false of the ledger from the day the ledger read that column mid-transaction. Rule 28 says the third instance means hunting the fourth, so every comment promising 'no window' or 'cannot drift' was listed and the candidates read in place: 'a reversals row is permanent and never updated' turns out to be TRUE, backed by no UPDATE policy and no function writing it
Reversals post counter-entries, so a reversed charge leaves both rows visible, and every counter-entry carries reverses_entry_id (065)

LANDED (066): THE GUEST LEDGER AGREES WITH THE BOOKS, PER FOLIO, AND THE CHECK RUNS ON DEMAND. folio_gl_reconciliation_folios gives one row per folio — the left side read from journal_entry_lines by role_key, the right computed independently from that folio's own charges, tax lines, discount applications and payments, less buckets naming what legitimately has not posted (pre_gl, pre_wiring, dependency, waiting, ready). ZERO TOLERANCE, stated as a decision: both sides are numeric(14,2) and every tax line was rounded when it was captured, so there is no irrational quantity for a tolerance to absorb, unlike the stock side's valuation_difference. On Heledon's live books it is exactly zero on every folio

LANDED (066): PER FOLIO RATHER THAN PER PROPERTY, and the deciding argument is not cost but blindness. A property total tells a duty manager at 7am that something is wrong; a folio row tells them which bill to open. And a property total can be GREEN while two folios are 5,000 out in opposite directions — rule 27's second shape one layer up. The headline is a SUM OVER the per-folio rows, never a second query, so it cannot contradict the breakdown, and it carries the worst single folio BY NAME with its figure

LANDED (066): and the one figure a per-folio read cannot see. outside_folios is the guest_ledger ACCOUNT total minus the folios that produced it, which catches a manual journal entry against the guest ledger and a mapping repointed after posting (1.1h4c). The account side is read by account_id while the folio side is read by role_key, deliberately: key them the same way and the two sides become one query and the check becomes vacuous

LANDED (066): the two SET-WISE forms the reconciliation needed, and the measurement that decided their shape. Calling 064's classifier once per document costs 20.2 SECONDS over a year of trading (4,000 folios, 17,800 documents, server-side, median of five) against 48 ms for folio_posting_states over the whole property; folio_totals_by_folio is 25 ms against 115 ms for the loop. The reconciliation itself is 768 ms for a year

LANDED (066): AND THE RE-EMISSION WAS BUILT, MEASURED AND REVERTED. folio_totals and folio_posting_state were to become thin filters over the set-wise forms so each rule existed once; measured side by side, that made the single-document classifier 18x slower (0.79 -> 14.14 ms) and folio_totals 193x slower (0.06 -> 11.10 ms) — on the two paths that can least afford it, since every posting helper classifies on every charge, discount and payment, and folio_totals is on every folio screen. Three fixes moved it 10.9 -> 14.1 ms without changing the shape, which is what says the cost is structural. So 064's and 021's forms stay authoritative and untouched, and assertions 1 and 3 pin the pair on EVERY live folio and EVERY live document — ON APPLY DAY, which is the honest limit of it. The reconciliation does NOT compute both implementations when it runs and cannot: pinning the classifier per document IS the 20-second path the inversion exists to avoid, so an inline pin would reinstate that cost on the one report somebody opens when something is already wrong. The standing check is SCHEDULED instead (1.1h2a), and until it ships this pair sits where 1.1h2a's does, a degree and a date better rather than a kind better

LANDED (066): folio_posting_states returns the DEPENDENCY'S STATE as a column, which is a performance fix that changed an answer's source and so carries its own assertion. Three branches ask 'is this counter's original in the books?', and self-joining the function's result put a CTE Scan inside a nested loop — a materialised CTE has no index — 5,402 loops over 8,900 rows, three times: the reconciliation did not finish inside a FIFTEEN-MINUTE timeout at 4,000 folios. The plan is what found it; the clock only said slow. Item 2b wants the column too, to post originals before counters

LANDED (066): 20 breakages, 18 red, and FIVE of the assertions were the broken thing rather than the code — the sixth time in this family of shipments. 13 carried its own copy of the discount formula and compared that to the entry (rule 27's first shape); its fixture used amounts where round-then-difference and difference-then-round COINCIDE (fourth shape), now 1,000 with 1.25 off where they differ by a kobo, re-checked each run so a changed VAT rate reports itself; 3 ran before the fixture reached never_dependency (third shape); 16 asked that one folio sorted first and passed when the ordering became opened_at, because now() is transaction start time so every fixture folio shares one; and 1 compared the balance pair on live folios, which have no payments, so a bulk reader that dropped payments entirely passed

LANDED (066): the expected-balance expression is computed ONCE. It was written three times in one select list — as the column, inside the difference, and inside the ordering — and dropping a bucket from the column left the DIFFERENCE reading its own untouched copy: the invariant stayed at zero while the figure beside it was wrong. Found by a breakage, not by reading

LANDED (064): A VOID POSTS A COUNTER-ENTRY, keyed as (folio_charge_void, the charge's id) on the same id, so it is findable from the thing it voided without a new table. The front desk keeps its one-click undo and the books stay append-only. It MIRRORS THE ENTRIES rather than rebuilding from the row — restate_charge_taxes rewrites a charge's tax rows on every discount, so a rebuild unwinds a figure the books never held — and the mirror spans the charge's DISCOUNT applications too, because voiding a charge takes its discount off the bill

LANDED (064): A DOCUMENT THAT MODIFIES OR UNWINDS ANOTHER NEVER POSTS UNLESS THAT OTHER ONE HAS POSTED, which closed a defect 062 and 063 left live in THREE reachable forms. Reversing a not-yet-due night posted its counter alone (guest ledger -48,444.75, revenue 45,023.00 Dr); discounting a pre-wiring charge posted 5,380.00 of relief against revenue never booked; reversing one posted 130,000.00 of revenue out of accounts it was never in. Every entry balanced internally, so nothing errored

LANDED (064): folio_posting_state — one function that says WHY a document is not in the books, as posted / ready / waiting_not_yet_due / waiting_for_dependency / never_pre_gl / never_pre_wiring / never_voided / never_dependency. THE PREFIX IS THE CONTRACT: waiting_* drains by itself, never_* does not. Every helper asks it, so the rule exists once; 1.1h4b's sweep posts what is ready and excludes never_*, and item 8's buckets absorb a document and its dependents together

LANDED (064): what the BILL says decides. A void removes the line (folio_totals filters it) so the ledger records nothing; a reversal leaves both rows showing so the ledger records both. The asymmetry was already in the product. The alternative argument — consistency with the stock ledger — was checked and does not apply: post_stock_adjustment REFUSES a forward date, so the stock side has no declined documents and no half-posted pairs

LANDED (068 + item 10): CHARGE CATEGORIES HAVE A SCREEN, and the database chose where it went. 044's trigger has refused a category with no revenue account since the day it shipped, and its hint read 'Open Settings, then Accounts, and choose the revenue account for this category' — naming a destination that did not exist. Rule 21 makes the hint the interface, so the tab is the fourth on the Accounts screen rather than somewhere that would have made the hint wrong. Adding 'Spa' or 'Conference hall' no longer means typing SQL

LANDED (item 10): THE PICKER CHOOSES A ROLE KEY AND SHOWS THE ACCOUNT. A category stores a key; what the money DOES is decided by the account that key points at, so 'Miscellaneous' without '4100 Other revenue' beside it is the silent choice this shipment ends. It offers ONLY keys that resolve to a live revenue account — an unmapped one is refused by PT424 on save, and a picker offering what the server will reject is the hint-names-the-wrong-remedy defect pointing the other way. It finds revenue keys by the ACCOUNT'S TYPE rather than a hardcoded list, so a tenant's own revenue_spa appears with no code change

LANDED (item 10): NO PREFILL, AND MISC IS A NAMED BUCKET OFFERED LAST. The field starts empty and every category names where it posts. Miscellaneous survives deliberately: deleting it would not remove the one-off charge, it would remove the honest place to put one, and the desk would bill it to Laundry at 11pm instead — a control that blocks legitimate work gets routed around rather than obeyed. Its expiry condition is 044's model and is written on 5.1: if Other revenue ever runs material in a month, the charges inside it have earned their own categories

LANDED (item 10): AND THE EMPTY STATE NAMES A REMEDY. On a fresh tenant with no revenue key mapped, the form does not render an empty picker — it says so and points at the tab beside it by its actual label. An empty state that names no remedy is a dead end, and this one is reachable on day one of every hotel

LANDED (item 10): the mapping tab gained the REVERSE DIRECTION — under each revenue account, the charge categories that post to it, folded from the same fetch rather than queried again so the two directions cannot disagree. A retired category is still listed and marked, because switching it off never moved the charges that used it. And 'nothing posts here' is rendered in WORDS and distinctly from 'not loaded yet': a revenue account nothing can be billed to is a setup mistake somebody must see, and the render proof's assertion 3.3 exists because three assertions about those cells reading correctly could not see that they said the same thing

LANDED (item 10): THE FOLIO'S FIRST RENDER PROOF — proofs/chargeCategoriesRender, 35 assertions, EIGHT breakages and all eight caught. It covers the three things SQL cannot reach: a role key shown without the account it resolves to, 'nothing posts here' rendered the same as 'not loaded yet', and the payment picker refusing to offer a method with no account while paymentMethodLabel still names 'other' so a historical payment does not render raw. It also pins 067's help text, which must never again invite a negative amount

LANDED (item 10, a finding from the breakages): breaking the FOLD left the CELL's assertions green — the cell was rendering a correct fold of a wrong map. That is why the proof tests the pure function beside the component instead of trusting it through the component, and the ordering fixture gives one account the code 4900 so that 'order by code' and 'misc last' give DIFFERENT answers: with every revenue account numbered below 4100, ordering by code alone puts misc last by accident and the ruling would have looked enforced when it was not
shipments.proof: Check a guest in, charge a room and a meal, take a part payment, apply a discount, reverse one charge, check out. The guest ledger and the receivable account agree to the naira, and every entry names the folio row it came from.
shipments.note: TWO PIECES ALREADY LANDED, both ahead of the wiring and for the same reason: each decides what a posting WRITES, so finding it afterwards means a correction migration against entries already in the books. 058 captured the tax; 059 captured the revenue account, gave a tax its own account, and split gl_wired_at. 059 also recorded the arithmetic that fixes the entry's shape — gross and discount as separate legs — and the three findings that are this shipment's to honour. The folio has been charging and taking payments since 021 and posting nowhere. Before go-live that is a gap; after go-live it is history to reconstruct. This closes it while there is still nothing to reconstruct. Also carries two commitments made when the spine shipped: the charge category form, because 044's guard protects a path that does not exist on screen yet, and the deletion of the revenue_misc fallback, because a silent default is fine while only SQL can reach it and wrong the moment a person can create a category from a screen.

shipments.t: A refused write says so, on every table that admin-gates one
ships: EIGHTEEN TABLES PUT is_tenant_admin IN UPDATE'S USING CLAUSE, and an UPDATE whose rows are filtered out by USING does not fail — it reports success and changes nothing. Measured on charge_categories before 068: a front_desk member's edit touched 0 rows and raised nothing. charge_categories, companies, company_rates, guests, inventory_categories, inventory_items, locations, media_assets, properties, property_finance_settings, property_settings, room_types, rooms, seasonal_rates, tax_charges, tenant_settings, tenants, units_of_measure

The fix is 068's, applied seventeen more times: the admin test moves to WITH CHECK so the statement raises instead of vanishing, with USING carrying the tenancy test the SELECT policy already uses. NOTHING NEW IS PERMITTED — the set of writes that succeed is identical, and only the set that failed silently moves to failing by name

And a bare RLS refusal names no remedy ('new row violates row-level security policy for table X'), so the tables whose screens matter get the 068 treatment: a named refusal from a BEFORE trigger saying who may do it and where

AND THE FIX DOES NOT WORK FOR DELETE, which is the limit of 068 as a worked example and is stated rather than inferred. FIVE admin-only DELETE policies — account_mappings, media_assets, properties, property_settings, tenant_settings — every one with the test in USING, because A DELETE HAS NO WITH CHECK for it to move to. All five are reachable by authenticated at the table level

AND NO TRIGGER CAN STAND IN FOR IT: RLS filters the row before a BEFORE DELETE trigger would fire. Measured on a throwaway table carrying a trigger that always raises — the non-admin's DELETE touched 0 rows and the trigger never fired, while an ADMIN's DELETE on the same table hit it with PT403, which is what proves the trigger could have fired and was simply never reached. So the only remedy for a DELETE is to stop exposing it: revoke it from the client roles and route deletes through an RPC that refuses by name

charge_categories has NO delete policy, so nothing deletes a category through PostgREST — not even an admin, by the same test. Retiring one (is_active) is the path and soft delete is the house rule (rule 5, §6). So 068 could not have demonstrated the DELETE case even had it tried, and that is exactly why this line carries the limit instead of leaving it to be read off the example

NOT a rename. The _member_ prefix on 39 of these policies is a TENANCY qualifier, not a permission one, and account_mappings's two _admin_ policies are the outlier. A census settled that before 068 renamed anything
shipments.proof: For each table: a non-admin UPDATE raises rather than touching zero rows, an admin UPDATE still lands, and the policy end state is read back from pg_policies rather than from the migration. For each of the five DELETE policies: the client roles can no longer reach DELETE at all, and the RPC that replaces it refuses by name. Every check with SET ROLE authenticated, because RLS is not enforced for the role a migration runs as and a test that skips it reads as proof.
shipments.note: FOUND WHILE SCOPING 1.1h4 ITEM 10, which was scoped on a report that charge_categories was not admin-gated at all. It already was — the report had read the policy NAMES instead of the expressions. What the behavioural check actually turned up was this, on eighteen tables. 068 fixes the one it owns and leaves the rest here rather than sweeping seventeen tables' policies inside a shipment about charge categories, which is the one-screen fix rule 23 warns about with the sign reversed.

shipments.t: The stock reconciliation's headline derives from its breakdown
ships: inventory_gl_reconciliation rebuilt as a SUM OVER inventory_gl_reconciliation_positions, instead of being its own independent query over the same movements

THE TWO CAN DISAGREE TODAY and nothing would notice. They are two implementations of one arithmetic: the property totals and the per-position breakdown each aggregate the movements themselves, so a change to one leaves the other reporting a different answer about the same stock — and whichever screen somebody happens to be looking at is the one they believe
